implemented_capabilities: skills/windows_app.py: WindowsAppSkill -- launch (subprocess.Popen, argv list, no shell=True, PATH/absolute .exe resolution with traversal rejection), focus (real pywin32 win32gui/win32process/win32api window enumeration + SetForegroundWindow, matched by executable basename or window-title substring), list_running (read-only visible-window enumeration: executable name + window title only, no content capture)

skills/filesystem.py: FilesystemSkill -- list/search (read-only, boundary-checked to the caller's home-directory tree via Path.resolve()+relative_to()), open (os.startfile). write/delete/move are NOT implemented: classify_risk() returns BLOCKED and validate() raises SkillValidationError for any such action rather than silently no-op'ing

skills/browser.py: BrowserSkill -- open_url/search via stdlib webbrowser only (no headless automation/scraping), strict http/https URL validation rejecting file://, javascript:, data:, and any other scheme

skills/terminal.py: TerminalSkill -- run_command via subprocess.run with real captured stdout/stderr/exit code and a configurable-but-capped timeout (default 30s, hard max 120s). classify_command() is a pure, deterministic BLOCKED > READ_ONLY > CONFIRM_REQUIRED classifier: a conservative denylist (format, del/rd/rmdir /s, Remove-Item -Recurse -Force, shutdown/Stop-Computer/Restart-Computer, diskpart, reg delete, net user, bcdedit, vssadmin, cipher /w, runas, sudo, takeown, remote iex/Invoke-Expression combined with a fetch construct, writes targeting C:\Windows\System32) checked before a narrow leading-verb READ_ONLY allowlist (dir/ls/type/cat/echo/whoami/pwd/cd/Get-ChildItem/Get-Process/Get-Content/git status|log|diff) that is disqualified entirely by any chaining/redirection operator (&, &&, |, ;, >, <), so a trick input like `dir & del /s` is BLOCKED via the denylist rather than slipping through as READ_ONLY

skills/obsidian.py: ObsidianSkill -- search/read wrapping the EXISTING memory.service.MemoryService (FTS5 + vault indexing), no reimplemented indexing/search. search preserves MemoryService's source/source_id provenance verbatim in ActionResult.data. read resolves a vault-relative path with the same resolve()+relative_to() boundary check as filesystem.py and reads the real file (MemoryService itself only exposes indexed snippets, not full note bodies)

skills/voice_bridge.py: build_action_request_from_voice(text, *, source, active_context=None) -> ActionRequest | None -- a small (4-pattern) deterministic phrase recognizer (focus <target>, open <url>, search for <query>, launch/open/start <app>) mirroring assistant/router.py's regex-based deterministic routing pattern (M2A acceptance criterion 12). Returns None for anything unrecognized so the caller falls through to the existing LLM/assistant path unchanged; does not modify assistant/router.py

skills/registry.py: SKILLS: dict[str, Skill] (eager, the 4 skills with no live-DB dependency: windows_app, filesystem, browser, terminal) and build_registry(memory_service=None, vault_path=None) -> dict[str, Skill] for the full 5-skill registry including obsidian once a live MemoryService is available (see known_gaps for why obsidian is not in the eager SKILLS dict)
known_gaps: pywin32's focus-by-window path (win32gui.SetForegroundWindow) was exercised against REAL win32 windows created in-process during the test run in this sandbox (tests/test_skill_windows_app.py's real_window fixture creates an actual off-screen top-level Win32 window via win32gui.CreateWindow and asserts win32gui.GetForegroundWindow() == hwnd after calling focus) -- this is genuine, observed pass, not a mock. It was NOT tested against a separate, independently-running foreground application (e.g. actually focusing a real Notepad process launched by a different process) in this sandbox session, since that would require popping/interacting with a real second-process GUI window during an automated test run. The underlying win32 API calls (SetForegroundWindow, ShowWindow, EnumWindows, GetWindowThreadProcessId, GetModuleFileNameEx) are the same regardless of which process owns the target window, so this is a reasonable-confidence gap, not a fabricated-working claim -- flagging it explicitly rather than omitting it.

terminal skill's execute() runs commands via subprocess.run(..., shell=True), which on Windows dispatches through cmd.exe. PowerShell-only cmdlets listed in the READ_ONLY allowlist (Get-ChildItem, Get-Process, Get-Content) will classify correctly but will FAIL at actual execution time with a real 'not recognized' error from cmd.exe unless the caller wraps them (e.g. `powershell -Command "Get-ChildItem"`) -- this is honest, observable behavior (a real FAILED ActionResult with real stderr), not a silent lie, but is worth the action runtime/HUD knowing about when surfacing PowerShell commands to the user.

filesystem skill's safe-root allowlist is deliberately minimal (just the caller's home directory tree, Path.home()) per the spec's 'small allowlist of safe roots' language -- it does not yet expose a way to add additional allowed roots (e.g. a project directory outside the home tree). Extending the allowlist, if needed, is a small, additive change to skills/filesystem.py's _safe_roots().

voice_bridge.py's phrase set is intentionally small (4 patterns: focus/open-url/search/launch) per the spec's 'a handful of phrase patterns, not a general NLU system' instruction -- it is not a substitute for the LLM path for anything more complex, by design.

skills/registry.py's SKILLS module-level dict does NOT include 'obsidian' (only windows_app/filesystem/browser/terminal) -- ObsidianSkill requires a live memory.service.MemoryService, which itself requires a live aiosqlite.Connection that this codebase only creates during app startup (app/main.py's lifespan, matching app/db.py's single-shared-connection design and app/deps.py's DI pattern). Constructing it eagerly at import time would mean opening an unmanaged second DB connection or fabricating a fake one to satisfy the constructor -- both rejected as dishonest/wrong per AGENTS.md's 'no fabricated success' rule. The action runtime should call skills.registry.build_registry(memory_service=<its own MemoryService instance>) once it has one (documented in skills/registry.py's docstring and in docs/coordination/handoffs/claude.md).
